figures.source: One oblique horseshoe magnet, two long rectangular arms ending openly at the left, curved joining body at the right; the rear upper arm is light, the nearer lower arm dark. End faces and body thickness are visible. One small rectangular wire loop hangs in the open gap near the left ends from one vertical textured strand extending to the top. Its nature as electrical lead versus suspension is not pixel-resolved. No pole letters, current arrow, normal, field arrow, dimensions, numbers, hand or natural object is visible.
figures.relations: Both arms belong to the same U-shaped body; the loop is between their open ends. The vertical strand reaches the upper edge of the loop. End faces and loop side edges are vertical in the projection. No polarity or loop-current direction can be derived from these unlabeled pixels.
figures.additions: Clean computed oblique projection and smooth sampled U bend; semantic-role shading replaces black halftone. No N/S, B, I, n, terminal or battery is added.
figures.routing: deterministic: all visible objects are manufactured apparatus with geometric relationships; no natural artwork is required.

figures.source: Left: a tall narrow projected circular loop with paired winding contours, two upper leads, a down arrow on the left upper lead and an up arrow on the right upper lead beside I. Downward current heads occur on the left loop side; an upward head occurs on the right side. The horizontal normal starts near the loop centre and points right, labeled vector n. Right: a physical screw/auger with vertical thick shaped handle, horizontal shaft, helical/thread-like marks and pointed right tip. A curved turning indicator around the shaft has a visible upward head at its lower-right portion. No hand, numerical angle or field arrow is visible.
figures.relations: The loop normal and screw shaft share a rightward projected axis. The visible left-down/right-up circulation is consistent with the right-hand screw advancing along the displayed normal. The 2D ellipse is not a true circular cross section in screen coordinates; do not assert screen-space perpendicularity.
figures.additions: One explicit orthographic model P(x,y,z)=(0.8x+0.6y,z); the loop lies in the y-z plane and its current-selected normal is +x. Its circulation is y=cos(t), z=sin(t), so y cross z = +x. Projection is a consistent reconstruction, not uniquely pixel-certified 3D. Smooth winding contours and clean thread marks are regularization, not turn/thread counts. Rotation is modeled with the same current sense.
figures.routing: deterministic: retain the actual screw handle, threaded shaft and tip, not an abstract replacement arrow.

figures.source: Two side-by-side objects: left a horizontal double-ended magnetic needle, S on the left light half and N on the right dark half, a concentric circular centre/pivot, and a small rightward arrow along the centreline toward N. Right a tall elliptical multi-contour coil with downward current heads on the left and upward current heads on the right. Its centre is a filled dot; a thick horizontal arrow from that centre points right and is labeled vector n. No external-field B label, support or dimensions is present.
figures.relations: The needle S-to-N arrow and the coil current-selected normal point right in the shared comparative frame. Pole placement determines S-to-N independently of any imagined magnet outside the figure. Current-to-normal derivation uses the same consistent projection as fig-243, not a guessed hidden arrowhead.
figures.additions: Readable S/N and vector n; semantic fill on the N half; regularized symmetric needle outline, three illustrative winding contours, not a measured turn count. Needle and loop are shown after stable settling in an approximately uniform external field, not during arbitrary rotation.
figures.routing: deterministic: exact pole ordering, direction agreement, current circulation and pivot/coil geometry.

figures.source: One suspended inclined circular multi-turn coil shown as several dark/light elliptical rim strokes, leaning from upper left toward lower right in the image. An upright inverted-U yoke surrounds its upper region; a vertical shaft continues from the arch top to a short thick horizontal top bar. Coil attachments are visible at the lower left and near the right upper side; the left has a small angular projecting bracket and the right joins the yoke and a wavy lead extending up-right to a thick free end. No current, n, B, pole, axis label, turn count, numerical dip or rotation arrow is visible.
figures.relations: Vertical suspension permits rotation about the vertical shaft; opposed coil bearings permit rotation about a horizontal physical axis which is oblique on the page. Do not call that screen line physically tilted or make it a second vertical axis. The inclined loop is not a measured dip angle. Electrical topology and any hidden second lead are unresolved and are not reconstructed.
figures.additions: Explicit orthographic camera with screen-right=(0.8,0.6,0) and screen-up=(-0.24,0.32,sqrt(0.84)); the horizontal bearing axis is world y, the vertical axis world z. A normalized illustrative tilt, not a source angle, places the coil in a plane spanned by y and (-sin(beta),0,cos(beta)). Two dashed axis guides and English labels are modern additions. No current-selected n or B direction is drawn: the unlabeled source cannot pixel-certify their signs. The text supplies stable Earth-field settling and field uniformity over a comparatively large coil.
figures.routing: deterministic: retain yoke, suspension bar/shaft, both bearings, angular left bracket and wavy right lead; no natural artwork or paid generation.
